Scottsdale bachelor party weekend: a 3-day itinerary

Scottsdale Sprinters plans a Scottsdale bachelor party weekend as three days with one anchor each: an arrival evening in walkable Old Town, a middle day that runs a golf morning or a pool afternoon and a night out after it, and a desert or lake day before the flights home. The group moves on one celebration vehicle rather than a convoy — the class seats 13 to 28 at $175–$295 per hour on a 4-hour minimum, so the shared ride starts between $700 and $1,180 before tax. Below: the itinerary, ideas by group type, where to stay by district, and the per-person arithmetic.

Last updated: September 17, 2026

What does a 3-day Scottsdale bachelor party weekend actually look like?

3 days, 3 anchors, and nothing else locked: an arrival evening in Old Town, a middle day that runs golf or pool by daylight and a night out after it, and a desert or lake day before the flights home. Scottsdale Sprinters moves the group between all 3. Day one is arrival. Flights land across a wide window, so the only fixed point worth setting is one evening in Old Town, the walkable district where dinner and the rest of the night sit a few blocks apart. Anyone landing late joins there rather than holding the group at the kerb. Day two is the day the weekend is remembered for. A tee time or a pool afternoon fills the daylight, the group resets at the lodging, and the evening runs back into Old Town with one vehicle staying with you rather than being re-summoned. Day three works better slow. A day out of the city — our Superstition Mountains & Apache Trail day, our Sonoran Desert Sunset run, or a Lake Pleasant day, each planned on its own tour page — gives the weekend a last shared thing that is not another night out, and puts everyone back in time to split by flight.

How does a bachelor party group move between all of it?

One celebration vehicle, booked for the block of hours you actually need. The class seats 13 to 28 on a shared 4-hour minimum at $175–$295 per hour: the Limo Party Sprinter (12-13 Pax) at the small end, the Party Bus (28 Pax) at the top, and 3 limo-cabin units between them. The vehicle earns its place on the legs that are not walkable: lodging to the course, lodging to Old Town, the day out of the city, and the ride back. Inside Old Town the block-to-block moves are quicker on foot than reloading a dozen people, and the chauffeur stages where it is legal to stand. Pick capacity off the table below, then tell the reservations team the real load. A seat count describes people, not clubs, coolers, gear bags or airport luggage, and the honest answer for a golf morning can differ from the one for the night after it.

What are the best Scottsdale bachelor party ideas by group type?

Three shapes cover almost every group: a golf group that wants tee times and a slow afternoon, a nightlife group that wants Old Town and a late return, and an adventure group that wants the desert or the water. Build the weekend around the day that matters most rather than trying to run all 3 hard. A golf group plans backwards from the earliest tee time and treats the rest of the day as recovery. Courses sit across North Scottsdale and the north-east edge of the city, far enough out that a shared vehicle beats a convoy of rentals. Book the course yourself; we move the group and the bags. A nightlife group wants Old Town, and Old Town rewards planning: the district is compact, the walk between confirmed stops is short, and the hard part is the end of the night. Decide the return rule before the first stop — one departure, or two waves with names against each. An adventure group gets out of the city. The desert north and east of Scottsdale, and the lake north-west of Phoenix, are day-trip distance, and each has its own tour page with its own plan. That is the day a chauffeured vehicle matters most: nobody drives a group back from open water at dusk.

Where should a bachelor party stay in Scottsdale?

Pick the district before the property. Old Town puts the evening within walking distance and shortens every late return. North Scottsdale trades that walk for space and quiet, and suits a golf-led weekend. A rented house anywhere in the city works for 28 or fewer if one address becomes the single pickup point. An Old Town base is the simplest weekend to run: the evening is a walk, the vehicle is only needed for the days out, and the late return is a short move. The trade is noise and a smaller footprint per person. A North Scottsdale base is the golf weekend's: closer to the courses, quieter between them, further from the evening. Budget a real transfer each way for a night out and put both directions in one booking. A rented house is the third shape, and its advantage is one door — one address, one ready time, one headcount. Whatever the district, give the reservations team the exact pickup address, the ready time and whether the property restricts where a large vehicle may stand. That last point decides whether the chauffeur is at the door or two streets away.

What does a Scottsdale bachelor party cost per person?

For the transport, the arithmetic is public: the celebration class runs $175–$295 per hour on a 4-hour minimum, so a booking starts between $700 and $1,180 before tax — roughly $36–$67 a head across a full vehicle. Everything else on the weekend is yours to set. Stretch that to the 5-hour evening the pricing page works through and the split lands at about $45–$83 a head: $45 in the Party Bus (28 Pax), $82 in the Pink Hummer Limo, $67 in the Limo Party Sprinter (12-13 Pax). You reserve the vehicle, not the seat, so a half-full booking costs the same and the per-head figure rises. Arizona sales tax of 8% is added at checkout, a 50% deposit confirms the vehicle, and the balance is charged to the card on file 48 hours before pickup. A one-way move is booked as a transfer instead, flat within 15 road miles from pickup to drop-off and priced from the drive beyond that, with the empty return included — $550 in the Party Bus (28 Pax). What this page will not do is put a number on the rest of the weekend. Lodging, tee times, meals and anything bought on the night are priced by whoever sells them: your other costs are yours to set. Add them to the transport figure above and request a current quote.

How does the desert or lake day work?

It runs as its own booked block rather than an extra stop on a night out. 3 of our tour pages carry that day and each states its own plan: Superstition Mountains & Apache Trail, Sonoran Desert Sunset and Lake Pleasant. Read the page for the one you want, then book the vehicle around it. A day out of the city is a different service shape from an evening in it: it starts earlier, runs longer, carries gear, and ends at the lodging. Treating it as its own line keeps the evening plan from quietly absorbing it. We move the group; the destination is the destination's own. Where a day involves water, a trail, a park or an operator, whatever that place requires is arranged with it directly and its current guidance controls. Send the confirmed timings with the quote request.

What are the house rules on board?

Three rules carry a fee: $1,500 for smoking or vaping on board, because the smell does not leave, $450 to deep-clean an excessive spill and $450 for a biohazard clean. An added stop on a transfer is $50, and nothing else is added to the base fare. The full list is published on the ride rules page. Arizona's rules for alcohol in a chauffeured vehicle are not ours to summarise loosely, so they have their own page: the Arizona alcohol law guide linked below answers that question and applies to every unit in this class. The rest is ordinary courtesy a bachelor party occasionally forgets. The chauffeur is working and stays out of the celebration. Aisles, doors and exits stay clear. Nothing leaves the vehicle into a place that prohibits it. And one person holds the manifest, so who is missing has an answer.

How do we get a written quote for the weekend?

Four steps: pick the vehicle from the table, send the dates with the full itinerary, confirm with a 50% deposit, and the balance is charged 48 hours before the first pickup. Every figure here is the published rate card; your own total comes back in writing. A quote needs the date and start time of each block, the pickup and final drop addresses, the stops between them, the passenger count, the bag and gear count, and how many hours you want the vehicle. If the weekend has a golf morning and a night out, describe both. Call or text (623) 986-6339, email reservations@scottsdalesprinters.com, or request a current quote on the pricing page. Name the unit if you know which one you want; the quote confirms it by name, with its rate, its minimum and the hours you asked for.

Frequently asked questions

How much does a Scottsdale bachelor party cost?

Scottsdale Sprinters can only price its own part of it: the celebration class runs $175–$295 per hour on a 4-hour minimum, so transport starts between $700 and $1,180 before tax, about $36–$67 a head across a full vehicle. Lodging, golf, meals and anything bought on the night are not ours to price: your other costs are yours to set. Request a current quote for your dates.

What are the best Scottsdale bachelor party ideas?

Scottsdale Sprinters groups them three ways: a golf-led weekend around North Scottsdale, a nightlife-led weekend around Old Town, and an adventure weekend built on a desert or lake day. Pick one as the anchor and keep the other two days loose.

What is a good 3-day Scottsdale bachelor party itinerary?

Arrival and an Old Town evening, then a golf morning or pool afternoon with a night out after it, then a desert or lake day before the flights. Scottsdale Sprinters books the vehicle as blocks against those three days rather than as one continuous hire.

How many people fit in a bachelor party vehicle?

The celebration class Scottsdale Sprinters books seats 13 to 28: the Limo Party Sprinter (12-13 Pax) at 13, the Pink Hummer Limo at 18, and the Party Bus (28 Pax) at 28, which is the ceiling. Every count is a seated count — nobody rides standing.

Is there an hourly minimum on a bachelor party booking?

Yes. Every celebration vehicle at Scottsdale Sprinters books on a 4-hour minimum, so a booking starts at the published hourly rate times 4 hours: $700 before tax in the Limo Party Sprinter (12-13 Pax), $1,000 in the Party Bus (28 Pax). A one-way move is booked instead as a transfer with no hour count: flat within 15 road miles from pickup to drop-off, priced from the drive beyond that with the empty return included.

Where should a bachelor party stay in Scottsdale?

Scottsdale Sprinters plans around districts rather than properties: Old Town if the evening should be walkable, North Scottsdale if the weekend is golf-led, or one rented house so the group has a single pickup address. We publish no lodging prices and recommend no property.

How does a golf group get to the course and back?

In the same celebration vehicle the rest of the weekend uses. Scottsdale Sprinters moves the group and the bags from the lodging to the course and back on a booked block of hours; you reserve the tee time yourself. Give the bag count with the headcount so fit is reviewed first.

Can we drink on board in Arizona?

Scottsdale Sprinters answers the Arizona alcohol rules on its dedicated guide, linked from this page, rather than paraphrasing them here. Three house rules carry a fee: $1,500 for smoking or vaping, $450 to deep-clean an excessive spill and $450 for a biohazard clean.

Can one vehicle cover the whole bachelor party weekend?

Often, but not always. Scottsdale Sprinters books the weekend as blocks, and a golf morning with clubs and an evening with none can price better as two. Send the whole itinerary and the written quote will say which shape costs less.

How do I book a bachelor party vehicle in Scottsdale?

Request a quote with your dates and itinerary on the pricing page, or call or text Scottsdale Sprinters on (623) 986-6339. A 50% deposit confirms the vehicle and the balance is charged to the card on file 48 hours before pickup. Arizona sales tax of 8% is added at checkout.
